turns.response_html:
Yes, Zoom meetings and webinars have a maximum number of participants that is determined by your account type and plan.

The limits vary significantly depending on whether you are hosting a standard Zoom Meeting, a Large Meeting (an add-on), or a Zoom Webinar/Event.

Here is a general overview of the typical limits for Zoom Meetings:

Zoom PlanStandard Meeting Participant LimitMax with Large Meeting Add-on
Basic (Free)100 participantsN/A
Pro100 participantsUp to 1,000
Business300 participantsUp to 1,000
Enterprise500 participantsUp to 1,000+

Key Details to Consider:

  • Standard Meetings (Basic/Pro/Business/Enterprise): These limits are the default for your account. You can purchase a Large Meeting add-on to increase this capacity, typically to 500 or 1,000 participants.
  • Zoom Webinars and Events: These products are designed for much larger audiences where attendees are primarily in view-only mode, and capacity can go up to 10,000+ attendees depending on the specific license purchased.
  • What Happens When the Limit is Reached? Once a meeting hits its participant limit, any new person attempting to join will receive a message saying the meeting has reached its maximum capacity. They can only join if another participant leaves.

To find your exact limit, you can sign in to the Zoom web portal, go to your Profile, and check the Account section where your meeting capacity is displayed.

turns.prompt_text: can zoom host private meetings and record videos that do not leave the desktop.
turns.response_html:
That's a great question, and the answer is Yes to both parts. Zoom provides specific features for hosting private meetings and for keeping the video files exclusively on your local computer.

1. Hosting Private Meetings

Zoom offers multiple security features that, when combined, make a meeting highly private and restricted:

  • Passcode: The most basic security measure; all participants must enter a passcode to join the meeting.
  • Waiting Room: This is often considered the best layer of privacy. Instead of joining directly, participants are placed in a virtual Waiting Room, and the host must manually admit them one by one. This prevents uninvited guests from joining even if they have the meeting ID and passcode.
  • Only Authenticated Users Can Join: You can configure the meeting to only allow users who are signed in to a Zoom account, or even more restrictively, signed in to a specific email domain (e.g., only people with @yourcompany.com email addresses).
  • Disable Join Before Host: Ensures no one can enter the meeting space until the host arrives.

By enabling the Waiting Room and requiring a Passcode, you establish a highly controlled, private environment.

2. Recording Videos That Do Not Leave the Desktop

This is achieved using Local Recording, which is a feature available on the Zoom desktop application (Windows, macOS, and Linux).

  • How it Works: When you start recording, you are prompted to choose where to save the file. You must select the option to "Record on this Computer" (Local Recording), rather than "Record to the Cloud" (Cloud Recording).
  • Desktop Only: The video and audio files are saved directly to a designated folder on the computer of the person recording (usually the host's "Documents/Zoom" folder by default).
  • No Cloud Upload: Since the recording is saved locally, it is never uploaded to the Zoom Cloud and does not rely on any Zoom servers for storage or access. This ensures the video files remain on your desktop and are only accessible by you.
  • Requirement: You must be using the Zoom desktop application to use the local recording feature.

🔒 Quick Guide to Keeping it Local

  1. Start your private meeting using the Zoom desktop application.
  2. Click the Record button in the meeting controls.
  3. Select "Record on this Computer."
  4. End the meeting. Zoom will then automatically convert and save the final video file (MP4) to a folder on your computer.

turns.prompt_text: How can videos be recorded on mac?
turns.response_html:
The Mac operating system provides several built-in tools for recording videos, whether you want to capture your screen, use your webcam, or both. The two primary native applications are the Screenshot toolbar (which includes screen recording) and QuickTime Player.

💻 1. Screen Recording (Recommended Method)

The fastest and most versatile way to record your screen and audio on a modern Mac (macOS Mojave or later) is using the Screenshot toolbar.

How to Use the Screenshot Toolbar

  1. Open the Toolbar: Press the keyboard shortcut Shift + Command + 5.
  2. Select Recording Type: A toolbar will appear at the bottom of your screen. Click one of the two video recording icons:
    • Record Entire Screen: Records everything on your display.
    • Record Selected Portion: Lets you drag a box to define a specific area to record.
  3. Adjust Options: Click Options to choose:
    • Save To: The location where the final video file will be saved (e.g., Desktop).
    • Microphone: Select your internal microphone to record your voice or an external one. (Note: By default, this tool cannot record Mac's internal system audio without a third-party driver like BlackHole.)
    • Timer: Set a delay before recording begins.
  4. Start and Stop:
    • Click the Record button (or click anywhere on the screen if recording the entire screen).
    • To stop, click the small Stop button (a square inside a circle) in the menu bar at the top of your screen, or press Command + Control + Esc.
  5. Edit: A small thumbnail of the recording will appear in the corner, allowing you to quickly click it to trim or mark up the video before it saves.

🎥 2. Webcam Video Recording (Movie Recording)

To record a video of yourself using your Mac's built-in camera (like the FaceTime HD Camera) or an external camera, you should use QuickTime Player.

How to Use QuickTime Player

  1. Open QuickTime Player: Find it in your Applications folder or use Spotlight Search.
  2. Start a New Movie: Go to the menu bar and select File > New Movie Recording.
  3. Configure Settings:
    • The video preview from your camera should immediately appear.
    • Click the small arrow next to the red Record button to select your desired Camera, Microphone, and Quality settings.
  4. Record and Save:
    • Click the red Record button to start.
    • Click the Stop button (black square) to end the recording.
    • Go to File > Save to choose a location and file name for your video.

📸 3. Simple Webcam Capture with Effects

For quick, casual webcam videos with fun effects and filters, you can use the Photo Booth app.

How to Use Photo Booth

  1. Open Photo Booth: Find it in your Applications folder.
  2. Switch to Video: In the bottom-left corner of the window, click the Video button (a small video camera icon) to switch from photo mode.
  3. Record: Click the red Record Video button to begin, and click the Stop button to finish. The video will be saved automatically within the Photo Booth application window, from where you can export or share it.

If you are interested in a more professional setup, you might consider third-party applications which offer more advanced features like integrated editing, simultaneous screen/webcam recording, and system audio capture. For a quick guide on recording your screen using the Mac's native feature, check out this video: How to Screen Record on a MacBook Pro (Quick & Easy Guide 2025).

turns.prompt_text: How can a webcam recording be easily made?
turns.response_html:
The easiest way to make a webcam recording depends on your operating system, as both Windows and macOS have simple, free, built-in apps designed for this task.

Using the native application is the quickest way because you don't need to download or install any extra software.

💻 1. On Mac: Use QuickTime Player

QuickTime Player is pre-installed on every Mac and is the simplest way to record a video of yourself using your built-in or external webcam.

  1. Launch QuickTime Player: Find it in your Applications folder or use Spotlight Search.
  2. Start New Movie Recording: In the top menu bar, go to File > New Movie Recording. Your webcam view should immediately appear.
  3. Check Settings (Optional): Click the small $\bigtriangledown$ arrow next to the red Record button to check that your desired Camera and Microphone are selected. You can also set the quality (High or Maximum).
  4. Record and Save:
    • Click the red Record button to start.
    • Click the Stop button (a black square) to finish the recording.
    • Go to File > Save to name the video and choose where to save the .mov file on your computer.

📸 2. On Windows: Use the Camera App

Windows 10 and 11 come with a Camera app that can record both photos and videos using your webcam.

  1. Launch the Camera App: Search for "Camera" in the Windows Start Menu.
  2. Select Video Mode: Once the app opens, click the Video icon (usually on the right side of the window) to switch from photo mode to video mode.
  3. Record and Stop:
    • Click the large Video button (the red circle) to start recording. A timer will start running.
    • Click the same button again to stop the recording.
  4. Find Your Video: The video is automatically saved to the Camera Roll folder within your Pictures library. You can click the thumbnail preview in the corner of the app to view or share it.

✨ 3. Using a Third-Party Tool

If you need more advanced features, such as combining your webcam feed with your screen, adding text, or using a virtual background, free third-party programs offer more creative control.

  • Clipchamp: A free, Microsoft-owned online video editor and webcam recorder that can be used in your browser (Chrome/Edge) or as a Windows app.
  • OBS Studio: A free, open-source program that offers a huge amount of flexibility for mixing multiple cameras, screens, and audio sources, but it has a steeper learning curve.

If you're on a Windows PC, this video provides a straightforward guide on how to use the built-in app: How to Record Video with Camera on Windows 10/11 (Windows Camera App).
